speaker_role: independent counselor (Empowerly College Counseling; former assistant director of admission at Brown University)
commercial_incentive: yes -- Empowerly is a paid college counseling service and the video promotes their blog/content funnel
key_insights: Request recommendation letters for summer program applications well in advance, via formal email plus an in-person follow-up, and include a resume
Match the recommender's subject area to the program (math/science teacher for STEM programs, English/history teacher for humanities programs)
Summer program essays should have a strong opening hook and directly address every part of a multi-part prompt
Admitted students to elite summer programs typically show a mission-driven, niche-focused extracurricular narrative rather than broad involvement

Highlighted five specific programs: COSMOS (CA, 4-week STEM residential), UC Santa Barbara's Research Mentorship Program (paired with a mentor for original research), Northwestern's Medill-Northwestern Journalism Institute/Cherub program (4-week, for rising seniors), LaunchX (entrepreneurship, multiple city/online tracks), and MIT's MITES program (6-week, underrepresented students in STEM)
Recommends checking application status near deadlines and giving recommenders a gentle reminder a week or two before the due date
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker states she was an assistant director of admission at Brown University for almost 14 years
COSMOS described as a 4-week program; MITES described as a 6-week program; Cherub/MNJI described as a 4-week program
notable_or_distinctive: Names five specific selective summer programs with concrete structural details (length, mentorship format, target students) rather than just generic 'do a summer program' advice.
reliability_notes: Produced by a paid counseling company (Empowerly) as marketing content, so program selection may be curated for engagement rather than comprehensiveness; program details are asserted without citation and could shift year to year.
